title: Four-month HPMZ (Study 31)
dek: 2HPMZ/2HPM: isoniazid, rifapentine, moxifloxacin, pyrazinamide. WHO (and CDC 2025) allow it for eligible people ≥12 with DS pulmonary TB. It is not BPaLM.
story: Study 31/A5349 showed a 4-month daily regimen of isoniazid, rifapentine (1200 mg), moxifloxacin, and pyrazinamide (2HPMZ/2HPM — PZA in the first two months) was non-inferior to 2HRZE/4HR for eligible pulmonary DS-TB. WHO made this a conditional recommendation for people aged ≥12. CDC/ATS/IDSA 2025 endorses the same skeleton as a preferred 4-month US option.

Eligibility is not a vibe: known or presumed drug-susceptible pulmonary disease, age gate, ability to take a fluoroquinolone and high-dose rifapentine, attention to drug–drug induction (rifapentine is still a CYP3A4 inducer). Extra-pulmonary disease, pregnancy, and many children under 12 are not this trial population.
Moxifloxacin here is a first-line companion. The same molecule is a Group A DR-TB drug in other sentences. Do not recycle a gyrA mutant into HPMZ because the acronym looks modern.
deep: Rifapentine 1200 mg daily is not 3HP’s 900 mg weekly. Different PK, different food effects, different interaction table.
PZA still occupies intensive-phase months. Hepatotoxicity monitoring does not retire.
HIV: the trial included people with HIV on compatible ART; dolutegravir dosing may need the rifamycin patch. Check the current overlay.
If FQ resistance is later found, this regimen is misbuilt. Baseline FQ testing is not optional intellectually even if programmes stagger it.

example.title: gyrA A90V after week 3 of HPMZ
example.setup: Started HPMZ on an Xpert RIF-not-detected pulmonary case. tNGS later: gyrA A90V, rpoB WT, katG WT.

steps.title: The M is inactive
steps.body: A90V is FQ-R. HPMZ’s moxifloxacin cannot be counted.

steps.title: Rebuild as DS-TB without FQ
steps.body: This is not RR-TB. Standard 2HRZE/4HR (or local SOP) is the usual rescue, not BPaLM.

steps.title: Ask how the FQ-R got there
steps.body: Prior FQ for pneumonia? Mixed infection? Either way, stop improvising moxi into DS-TB.

example.takeaway: HPMZ is a DS-TB 4-month recipe that assumes a live FQ.

check.prompt: In WHO 2HPMZ/2HPM, the P and M are:
check.why: Do not confuse with BPaLM’s Pa = pretomanid.

check.prompt: Study 31 rifapentine intensive-phase daily dose is 1200 mg. 3HP weekly rifapentine is 900 mg. These are:
choices: Different regimens (daily high-dose RPT vs weekly TPT) and must not be swapped
check.answer: Different regimens (daily high-dose RPT vs weekly TPT) and must not be swapped

check.prompt: On the HPMZ hierarchy, why is BPaLM in the “Not this” row?
choices: Because HPMZ is a DS-TB rifapentine–moxifloxacin 4-month regimen; BPaLM is a 6-month RR-TB regimen with a different P (pretomanid)
Because WHO forbids moxifloxacin in all TB
check.answer: Because HPMZ is a DS-TB rifapentine–moxifloxacin 4-month regimen; BPaLM is a 6-month RR-TB regimen with a different P (pretomanid)
